steps.label: Variables and Decisions
steps.content:
Year 6 Scratch

Variables and Decisions

Year 6, 6.2.3

  • Store and change values with variables.
  • Compare values and choose with if then else.
  • Build a clicker game and a catching game that check themselves.

steps.label: Variables Store Values
steps.content:
Variables Store Values

A variable is a named place that stores a value that can change while the game runs.

  • Make one in Variables with Make a Variable. Give it a clear name, like score.
  • set [score] to (0) gives it a value. Do this when the green flag is clicked.
  • change [score] by (1) adds to it. A negative number takes away.
  • The box on the stage shows its value while the game runs.
when flag clicked
set [clicks v] to (0)

when this sprite clicked
change [clicks v] by (1)

steps.label: Check: Follow the Variable
steps.content:
Check: Follow the Variable

These are the two scripts from the last slide.

steps.label: Activity 1: Gem Clicker
steps.content:
Activity 1: Gem Clicker

Work on your own. Count clicks in a variable and reward the player at 10.

Build it

  • Make a variable called clicks. The green flag sets it to 0 and the costume to gem.
  • Each click on the Gem adds 1 to clicks.
  • At 10 clicks the Gem turns gold, not before.
  • Each click says Keep going! or You win!, using if then else.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: Comparisons and If Else
steps.content:
Comparisons and If Else

A comparison is a condition: it reports true or false.

  • (score) > (9) is true when score is more than 9.
  • (score) < (10) is true when score is less than 10.
  • (score) = (10) is true only when score is exactly 10.
  • if then else runs the top part when the condition is true, and the bottom part when it is false. Never both.
if <(clicks) < (10)> then
say [Keep going!]
else
say [You win!]
end

steps.label: Check: True or False
steps.content:
Check: True or False

score is 10.

items.prompt: Which of these conditions is true when score is 10?
items.explain: 10 is not more than 10 and not less than 10. It is equal to 10.

items.prompt: An if then else block has a false condition. Which blocks run?
options: The blocks in the else part
The blocks in the top part
items.explain: False means the else part runs. The top part is skipped.

steps.label: Fruit Catcher Toolkit
steps.content:
Fruit Catcher Toolkit

Blocks for the next challenge. Work out where each one goes.

go to x: (pick random (-200) to (200)) y: (170)

if <(y position) < (-170)> then
change [lives v] by (-1)
end
  • pick random gives a different number each time, so the Apple drops from a new place.
  • y position < -170 is true when the Apple reaches the bottom: a miss.
  • A catch is touching [Bowl]?.
  • When lives reaches 0 the game is over.

steps.label: Activity 2: Fruit Catcher
steps.content:
Activity 2: Fruit Catcher

Work on your own. The starter project has the Bowl and the Apple.

Build it

  • The arrow keys move the Bowl. The green flag sets score to 0 and lives to 3.
  • The Apple starts at the top at a random x, then falls.
  • A catch adds 1 to score. A miss takes 1 from lives. Either way the Apple goes back to the top.
  • When lives reaches 0 the game ends.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.
